title: Hydrogen cyanide determination in cassava leaves using the picrate paper method
author: Matema LE Imakumbili
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2dxga7n

steps.title: Set up work area
steps.instruction: Arrange a bench or table with the mortar, pestle, scissors, paper napkins, and all contents of the Protocol E kit. Clean the mortar, pestle, and scissors before starting. Keep a refrigerator nearby for leaf and picrate paper storage, and provide a wash area (sink or bucket with water and brush) for cleaning the mortar and pestle after each sample.

steps.title: Prepare leaf sample
steps.instruction: Remove petioles if only leaf blades are to be analysed. If the leaf quantity is large, sub‑sample by cutting each leaf into inner, middle and outer sections, chopping each section into ~1 cm × 1 cm pieces, mixing the pieces, and selecting a small, representative amount that can be ground quickly. Place the selected pieces in the mortar and grind immediately to avoid cyanide loss. If leaves are few and small, cut and grind directly without sub‑sampling.

steps.title: Weigh 100 mg leaf material
steps.instruction: Weigh exactly 100 mg of the freshly ground leaf using a 0.0001 g (0.1 mg) analytical balance in the laboratory, or a portable plastic balance supplied in the kit (which has a 100 mg weight glued inside a spoon) if working in the field.

steps.title: Add sample to bottle with buffer
steps.instruction: Place a round filter‑paper disc pre‑loaded with buffer at pH 6 into a flat‑bottomed plastic bottle (provided). Add the 100 mg ground leaf, then add 1 mL of distilled water (or bottled water if distilled is unavailable).

steps.title: Insert picrate paper
steps.instruction: Add a yellow picrate paper attached to its plastic strip into the bottle without letting the paper touch the liquid. Orient the strip so the longer side faces downwards, close the bottle with the screw‑cap lid.

steps.title: Prepare blank sample
steps.instruction: Set up another bottle exactly as above but add no leaf material; include the buffer‑loaded filter paper, water, and the yellow picrate paper, then cap.

steps.title: Prepare control/standard
steps.instruction: In a third bottle place a filter‑paper disc loaded with buffer and linamarase, add a linamarin paper, add 0.5 mL water, insert the yellow picrate paper (long side down), and screw the cap on.

steps.title: Incubate bottles
steps.instruction: Leave all bottles standing for 16–24 h at room temperature (20–35 °C) in the dark (e.g., a cupboard). On cooler days you may extend incubation to the full 24 h.

steps.title: Dry picrate papers
steps.instruction: After incubation, open each bottle, carefully remove the picrate papers still attached to their plastic strips, and place them on the screw‑cap lids or on A4‑size paper to dry. Label each paper (or the A4 paper) with its identity. Keep the papers dry and avoid touching the reacted side.

steps.title: Read colour against chart
steps.instruction: Match the colour of the uncovered side of each dried picrate paper to the supplied colour chart and record the cyanide concentration (ppm). Verify that the blank reads zero and the control gives the expected value. If desired, later obtain spectrophotometric readings from the same papers.

steps.title: Transport and store reacted papers (optional)
steps.instruction: If spectrophotometric analysis will be performed later, wrap each reacted picrate paper individually in Glad‑wrap or a small plastic bag (≈2 cm × 10 cm), keep them away from light, place them in an opaque, cool container, and transport quickly. Upon arrival at the laboratory, store the papers in a deep freezer; they remain stable indefinitely but should be measured within 1–2 days for best accuracy.

steps.title: Extract colour for spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Remove the plastic backing sheet from a dried picrate paper, place the paper in a test tube (or a 25–50 mL beaker) and add exactly 5.0 mL water measured with a pipette.

steps.title: Develop solution
steps.instruction: Swirl gently and let the tube stand at room temperature for about 30 min, giving occasional gentle stirring.

steps.title: Remove paper after extraction
steps.instruction: After 30 min, use a plastic disposable knife to lift the picrate paper out of the tube (do not use metal or suction tools). The colour should have been fully transferred to the solution.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 510 nm
steps.instruction: Zero the spectrophotometer with the solution from the blank (step 6). Measure and record the absorbance of each sample solution at 510 nm.

steps.title: Calculate cyanide concentration
steps.instruction: Calculate total cyanide (ppm fresh weight) using Equation 1: cyanide (ppm) = 396 × absorbance.

steps.title: Validate results
steps.instruction: Confirm that the cyanide values obtained from the colour chart and from the spectrophotometer are comparable and that the control (standard) matches the expected value.

steps.title: Reuse plastic backing (optional)
steps.instruction: After extraction, carefully remove and clean the plastic backing sheet; it may be washed and reused for future picrate papers.
